aboutH2: Birch Wellness Center: Outpatient Counselling in Downtown Winnipeg
intro: Birch Wellness Center is a private outpatient wellness centre located in Winnipeg, Manitoba. Birch Wellness Center specializes in the treatment of mental health, substance, drug and alcohol abuse.

Birch is a group practice, not a treatment program you live in. Close to twenty independent practitioners share a heritage house at 34 Carlton Street, including clinical psychologists, Canadian Certified Counsellors, registered social workers, registered psychiatric nurses, an addictions counsellor with lived experience of recovery, and practitioners of acupuncture and osteopathy. You come in for appointments and go home afterwards.

pillars.title: A Heritage House on Carlton Street
pillars.body: Birch works out of a turn-of-the-century house at 34 Carlton Street, between Broadway and Assiniboine Avenue in downtown Winnipeg. The rooms keep their original woodwork and stained glass, and the waiting areas feel more like a living room than a clinic. The Legislative Building, Osborne Village, the Exchange District and The Forks are all close by, and several main bus routes stop nearby. Parking is on Carlton Street or the side streets, paid through the PayByPhone app, and the lot behind the house is for staff only.

pillars.title: Appointments Instead of a Residential Stay
pillars.body: Birch says plainly in its FAQ that it is not an in-patient or residential treatment centre and only provides outpatient, private services. There is no set program length. You book sessions with one practitioner, usually by the hour, and keep going for as long as it helps. Many practitioners also see clients by video or phone, and some offer evening or weekend times. Because the practice works with individuals of all ages, couples, families and groups, a partner or family member can be seen too. If you need medical withdrawal management or a live-in program, you would arrange that elsewhere and could use Birch for counselling alongside or afterwards.

pillars.title: Independent Clinicians Who Refer to Each Other
pillars.body: Louise Blanchard, a Canadian Certified Counsellor with more than 30 years in practice, founded Birch and still sees clients there. Each practitioner runs their own practice and sets their own fees, but they meet for consultation and refer between themselves, so a client seeing a counsellor for drinking can also see a psychologist for trauma or a psychiatric nurse in the same building. Addiction work is listed by Louise Blanchard, Dr. Phoenix Gillis, addictions counsellor Amber Dittberner, Stephan Warrener and several social workers and nurses. Many of the team also teach or research at the University of Manitoba and the University of Winnipeg.

overview: Birch Wellness Center opened in 2013 in a heritage house on Carlton Street. It brings together independent practitioners in clinical psychology, counselling and psychotherapy, psychiatric nursing, clinical social work, relationship and family therapy, child and youth therapy, osteopathy and acupuncture. For addiction, that means one-to-one counselling for alcohol, drug, gambling and other addictions, help with mental health problems that come with them, and family or couples sessions when the people close to you want support too.

location.heading: Birch Wellness Center in Winnipeg, Manitoba
location.intro: Birch Wellness Center is in downtown Winnipeg, in a heritage house on Carlton Street between Broadway and Assiniboine Avenue, a few blocks from the Legislative Building and The Forks. From outside the city, Selkirk is about 35 minutes away by car, Steinbach about 50 minutes, Portage la Prairie about an hour and Brandon roughly two and a quarter hours along the Trans-Canada.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's own website and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is Birch Wellness Center a residential rehab?
faqs.a: No. Birch's own FAQ says it is not an in-patient or residential treatment centre and only provides outpatient, private services. You see a counsellor, psychologist, social worker or psychiatric nurse for appointments at the Carlton Street house, or by video or phone, and you live at home throughout.

faqs.q: How much do sessions at Birch Wellness Center cost?
faqs.a: Fees run from $60 an hour with a supervised practicum student to $225 an hour with a registered clinical psychologist, according to the centre's FAQ. Each practitioner sets their own rate, and many offer a sliding scale or payment plan for people with limited income. Ask the person you book with about their fee.

faqs.q: Does Manitoba Health or my insurance cover it?
faqs.a: Manitoba Health does not cover psychologists or counsellors, so sessions at Birch are paid privately. Most extended health plans cover clinical psychologists, certified counsellors, psychotherapists and clinical social workers, and some cover osteopathy and acupuncture. You pay at each visit and send the receipt to your insurer unless your practitioner has set up direct billing.

faqs.q: Who does addiction counselling at Birch?
faqs.a: Several practitioners list addictions as a service, including founder Louise Blanchard, psychologist Dr. Phoenix Gillis, counsellor Stephan Warrener and addictions counsellor Amber Dittberner. Amber Dittberner works with alcohol, drug and gambling problems as well as internet, sex and spending addictions. Her profile lists an Applied Counselling Certificate in addictions from the University of Manitoba, more than nine years of sobriety and 12-step work with clients.

faqs.q: Does Birch Wellness Center offer detox?
faqs.a: No. Birch only offers outpatient appointments, so there is no medical detox or overnight care. If you need help to stop drinking or using safely, start with your doctor or Manitoba's public addiction services through Shared Health, then use Birch for counselling alongside or afterwards.

faqs.q: Do I need a referral to book?
faqs.a: No referral from a physician is needed unless a particular practitioner asks for one. Some insurance plans do want a referral before they reimburse you, so check with your insurer before your first appointment to avoid delays.

faqs.q: How do I book an appointment?
faqs.a: Call 204-505-0325, extension 100, and the office assistant will pass your request to the practitioner you want. New clients who are not sure who to see are matched by the office assistant or by founder Louise Blanchard. Reception answers Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 4:30pm.

faqs.q: Where is Birch Wellness Center and where do I park?
faqs.a: Birch is at 34 Carlton Street in downtown Winnipeg, between Broadway and Assiniboine Avenue, and several main bus routes run close by. Street parking on Carlton, Assiniboine, Hargrave, Edmonton and Broadway is paid through the PayByPhone app, and there is a public lot at Edmonton and Broadway about half a block away. The lot behind the house is for staff only.

faqs.q: Can I have sessions online, in the evening or on weekends?
faqs.a: Yes, with some practitioners. The centre says many offer virtual or phone sessions and some see clients in the evening or at weekends, so ask the person you book with about their hours.

Most practitioners do not charge if you cancel at least 24 hours ahead. Same-day cancellations are usually billed at half the fee, except in emergencies, and a no-show is billed at the full rate. Confirm the policy with your own practitioner.
